Replay

Authenticated P2P links

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Ownership and bounds

Use this experimental transport wrapper to authenticate and encrypt a physical connection between two provisioned member incarnations. The native P2P Direct owner connects it to party provisioning and Duel's ENet transport.

The trusted service derives a pair key from the two enrollment keys using Odin's HKDF-SHA256 implementation. The derivation binds the entire match scope and the two sorted member/incarnation identities. A pair never receives the other member's enrollment key. Changing either incarnation changes the pair key; an unchanged service restart does not. The key is provisioned through a confidential channel.

Each connection exchanges fresh 32-byte nonces under pair-key HMAC proofs. The transcript derives separate directional/channel traffic keys and separate confirmation keys. Confirmation/ack retry handles a lost final handshake message; an authenticated data packet can also confirm possession of the transcript keys. Every gameplay packet uses the standard ChaCha20-Poly1305 implementation, with its header as associated data. No packet reaches the game before authentication.

The construction uses HKDF and ChaCha20-Poly1305 from Odin's core crypto packages. The surrounding Replay handshake/framing is new and is not a standard protocol or an independently reviewed security claim. This PSK construction does not provide forward secrecy against later enrollment-key/service compromise.

Ownership and bounds#

  • open takes a trusted Grant, the local identity, physical peer, fresh cryptographic nonce, clock and already-connected generation-aware transport. A nonce must never be reused for another open. Do not serialize/copy a live Link.
  • Supply a dedicated route for this peer, for example through transport.Router. pump consumes its route. Unrelated sender packets are refused, not forwarded.
  • transport exposes the common transport interface. identity exposes the remote identity only after admission. It does not create a gameplay roster.
  • close clears keys and pending plaintext; it does not close the borrowed base. The embedding owns the underlying connection's lifetime.
  • A changed transport generation or disconnected base fails the link and drops pending plaintext. A replacement connection needs a fresh provider decision and fresh link nonce; it cannot silently inherit the prior admission.
  • Handshake timeout is explicit (250–120000 ms). Receive work is bounded to 32 packets per pump, plus one retained plaintext packet. Buffer_Too_Small retains that packet until a sufficient read or connection retirement.
  • Overhead is 32 bytes; plaintext limit is transport.MAX_PACKET_BYTES - 32. Counters and 64-packet replay windows are separate for reliable/unreliable channels. Reliable delivery must preserve per-direction order. Unreliable packets older than the replay window are discarded.
  • Every encryption consumes a sequence, even if the base reports backpressure. A retry cannot encrypt different plaintext with a previously used key/nonce.

The grant records the identities approved by the provider when it was issued; it does not detect later revocation while offline. Before binding a new connection, the embedding must refresh admission. It must retire existing links when authenticated notices report a newer incarnation or revocation. A shared pair secret authenticates the connection between those participants, but does not let either participant judge the other's simulation as a trusted referee.

tests/replay_p2p_link/run.sh currently passes seven native tests and WASM checking: scope/identity key separation, handshake faults, encrypted bidirectional traffic, tampering/replay/reflection/channel substitution, retained receive buffers, generation replacement, channel-window independence, bounded denial and nonce consumption under backpressure. The native party fixture additionally exercises real encrypted ENet gameplay and connection replacement after a process kill.
